GOAL (design review Step 7): the set of reveals that exact matching can grant must no longer be bounded by the narrator's four-item prompt projection. Today KnowledgeProjector._candidates (knowledge.py) keeps only max_candidates=4 eligible reveals (sorted by entity reference, priority, id), and cloudflare.py runs uniquely_matched_authored_handoff, _shadow_matched_candidate_id, _handoff_eligible_candidate_ids and the semantic fallback over that truncated tuple. So a fifth eligible reveal can never be matched even by an exact command. Fix that without changing the narrator prompt content or any semantic policy.

READ FIRST: storygame/runtime/knowledge.py (TurnKnowledgeContext, KnowledgeProjector.project/_candidates), storygame/runtime/cloudflare.py (assemble_turn_prompt, _shadow_matched_candidate_id, _model_candidates, _handoff_eligible_candidate_ids, _semantic_authored_handoff, _semantic_no_clue_rules, _legacy_projection_candidates), storygame/runtime/candidate_matcher.py, tests/test_design_review_fixtures.py (the 'more than four eligible' fixture currently pins the defect as CURRENT DEFECT; update it to assert the fix), tests/test_cue_escalation.py, tests/test_attempt_bundle.py.

BUILD:
1. knowledge.py: TurnKnowledgeContext gets a new field (e.g. reveal_universe: tuple[RevealCandidate, ...], default empty) holding ALL eligible reveals in the same sort order, uncapped. `candidates` stays capped at max_candidates and is what the narrator prompt shows; its content and order must stay byte-identical.
2. cloudflare.py: exact matching (uniquely_matched_authored_handoff, the shadow match, and the handoff-eligible id set) runs over the full reveal_universe. The narrator's candidate list stays the capped `candidates` minus handoff-eligible ids (computed from the universe), so prompts are unchanged for every case that had four or fewer eligible reveals. Fall back to `candidates` if reveal_universe is empty (old test doubles).
3. Semantic fallback keeps its own bounded shortlist (the existing cap of 6 and 40-call budget are unchanged, no policy change), now drawn from the universe in sort order instead of from the four-item projection. Do not change the question sent to the model or the negation guard.
4. Telemetry: provider attribute `last_reveal_selection` (a plain dict, reset every turn in assemble_turn_prompt) with key `outcome` set to exactly one of: `exact_match`, `semantic_match`, `no_eligible_action` (no reveal in the universe has action evidence plus delivery text and is unestablished), `shortlist_exclusion` (the semantic shortlist cap left out at least one eligible reveal and nothing matched), `exact_tie` (the exact matcher found two or more candidates tied and returned None; detect this without changing the matcher's public return), `semantic_refusal` (model ran, returned zero or more than one id), `provider_error` (semantic call raised), `budget_exhausted` (semantic call budget of 40 spent and it would otherwise have run). Also keys `matched` (id or None), `universe_size`, `shortlist_size`. Precedence when several apply: exact_match, exact_tie, then the semantic outcomes, then no_eligible_action. Existing last_semantic_match must keep working unchanged.
5. Tests in tests/test_reveal_universe.py, hermetic, real engine state, stubbed provider/semantic_ask, under 15 s: (a) real 1A state with five eligible reveals (see the fixture in tests/test_design_review_fixtures.py, `k_sl_1a_c_r2` is dropped by the 4-cap): an exact command for the fifth reveal now produces an authored handoff for it; (b) the narrator prompt candidate ids and order are identical to before for that state (assert against the capped list); (c) one test per telemetry outcome listed above, each asserting the exact `outcome`; (d) positive, wrong-target, partial-action and ambiguous commands over real reveals keep their previous grant/no-grant result; (e) request reconstruction: assemble_turn_prompt twice for the same state and input gives equal prompts and equal last_reveal_selection.
6. Hard rules: story-agnostic runtime, no network, no prose-as-truth. Narrator-facing strings: you add none and change none.

HOW TO RUN: confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)"` prints a path inside the cwd. Tests: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_reveal_universe.py, then the full suite with -n auto. Ruff: PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix . and -m ruff format . . Reply with the files changed.
